text: CHAPTER 26
speaker: Narrator

text: Impossible Lines
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: They descended through the stairwell's impossible dark and stepped into the First City.
speaker: Narrator

text: Or what remained of it.
speaker: Narrator

text: The scale hit first, and it hit wrong. Streets wider than any avenue in Uruk opened ahead of them, yet the buildings pressed too close, leaning out over the thoroughfares like men bent forward to eavesdrop. Towers rose at angles that should have brought them down centuries ago, upper stories jutting out in layers that made no architectural sense. Bridges crossed themselves in midair—vanishing into one structure and emerging from another several stories higher, as if the city had been built by someone who had only ever heard geometry described secondhand.
speaker: Narrator

text: Every surface carried the same dull, oily sheen as the wall they had pressed against above. Torchlight sank into the stone rather than reflecting from it. The air tasted of dust and something colder, like the inside of a sealed jar that had never been opened.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag stopped three paces past the threshold.
speaker: Narrator

text: This isn't a ruin,
speaker: Balag

text: he said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Ninsun was already turning in a slow circle, eyes moving from street to arch to impossible bridge.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: No. Ruins collapse according to rules. This is still following rules. Just not ours.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu said nothing. She was staring upward at a colonnade that continued past the point where any supporting wall should have ended. Her expression was not fear. It was calculation.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik looked back.
speaker: Narrator

text: The stairwell they had descended was gone. In its place stood a solid wall of the same dark stone, seamless, as if the passage had never existed. The only evidence they had come from above was the cold still clinging to their clothes and the faint vibration of the mark on his palm.
speaker: Narrator

text: They were inside.
speaker: Narrator

text: No one stated the obvious.
speaker: Narrator

text: They moved carefully along the nearest street. The paving stones were large and fitted with the same impossible precision they had seen on the buried road above. No weeds grew between them. No dust had collected in the joints. The city looked abandoned and yet maintained, as though something still walked these streets after the living had left.
speaker: Narrator

text: Doorways stood too narrow for the buildings they belonged to. Along one wall a row of shallow niches faced downward instead of outward, each the size of a household altar. Names had been scratched out of the lintels above several entrances, the cuts deep and deliberate, as if the act of erasure had mattered more than the names themselves.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun stopped at the first intersection and crouched beside a low wall. Carved into the stone at regular intervals were the same incomplete spiral-drop symbols they had seen on the door above. Seven of them. Each slightly different. Each facing a different direction.
speaker: Narrator

text: The gates,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said quietly.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Not metaphors. Actual thresholds. The tablets weren't describing a journey through the underworld. They were describing a map.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik studied the nearest carving. The spiral was unfinished in the same place as the one above. A deliberate omission.
speaker: Narrator

text: What does incomplete mean?
speaker: Zik

text: he asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Ninsun shook her head.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The texts disagree. Some say each gate took clothing, then rank, then name. Others mention memory. One damaged tablet claims the last gate took whatever remained of the traveler that still made them recognizable as themselves. The incomplete mark could mean the threshold is still closed. Or that it is waiting for the missing piece. I can't tell which version is older.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag's hand rested on the haft of his axe.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then we don't give it anything.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu laughed once, low.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You think it asks politely?
speaker: Enhedu

text: They continued.
speaker: Narrator

text: The deeper they walked, the more the geometry refused to settle. A street that appeared straight when viewed from one end curved sharply when they reached its middle. A courtyard they passed on their left reappeared on their right ten minutes later, identical down to a cracked basin in its center. Zik tried marking their path with small stones. When he looked back, the stones were gone.
speaker: Narrator

text: Or they had never been placed.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun kept a running record on a scrap of parchment, noting every turn, every symbol, every impossible junction. After the third time the same courtyard returned, she stopped writing.
speaker: Narrator

text: The map is changing as we move,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Or we are changing relative to it. I can't tell which.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik opened the journal.
speaker: Narrator

text: The pages that had once shown the cross-section of the city beneath Uruk were different now. The upper layers—the desert, the outpost, the first staircase—had faded almost to invisibility. In their place the ink had thickened into a dense network of streets, chambers, and descending lines that continued far past the edge of the paper. At the center of the densest tangle the spiral-drop symbol appeared again, complete this time, and larger than any they had seen.
speaker: Narrator

text: Beneath it, in his father's hand:
speaker: Narrator

text: THE SECOND DOOR IS NOT A DOOR.
speaker: Bel-iddin

text: Zik closed the book before anyone else could read it. The choice surprised him even as he made it. The knowledge felt private, like a debt that belonged only to him.
speaker: Narrator

text: They found the first living thing an hour later.
speaker: Narrator

text: Or what had once been living.
speaker: Narrator

text: A figure stood in the center of a wide plaza, facing a blank wall rather than the open space. Its feet were fused into the paving stones as if the city had grown around them. The body itself seemed assembled from several architectural surfaces—part column, part lintel, part threshold—rather than carved as a single statue. It wore the remains of a linen robe so old the fabric had fused with the dust that covered it. Around its neck hung a single bead of black glass, identical to the one Balag had left at the well.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun exhaled slowly.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: A gatekeeper.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Is it dead?
speaker: Enhedu
